summary: Code review FAIL. One Blocking issue: the CSS opacity separator trick in .health-alert-issue + .health-alert-issue (lines 1308-1315) is dead code. `opacity: calc(1/0.6)` on `> *` clamps to 1.0 (CSS opacity is bounded [0,1]) and has no effect. All issue rows after the first render at 60% opacity — text and buttons both dimmed. The developer comment 'restore to 1 relative to parent' documents behavior that the CSS spec does not support. Fix is 3 lines: remove opacity:0.6, remove the > * rule block, change border to var(--color-border-light) for a clean neutral separator. All four acceptance criteria are otherwise met — the layout, badge, theming, and custom properties usage are all correct.

comments.note: BLOCKING: The opacity separator trick in .health-alert-issue + .health-alert-issue is dead code based on a CSS misunderstanding. CSS opacity is NOT a channel alpha — it creates an off-screen stacking context. Setting opacity: 0.6 on the parent means all rendered children are composited at 60% opacity. The `> *` rule `opacity: calc(1/0.6)` clamps to 1.0 (since CSS opacity is bounded [0,1]) and therefore has zero effect on the final rendered opacity. The comment 'restore to 1 relative to parent' documents behavior that does not occur. Consequence: all issue rows after the first display with 60%-opacity text and buttons — unintended and degrading to readability. Fix (3 lines): remove the `opacity: 0.6` declaration, remove the entire `.health-alert-issue + .health-alert-issue > *` rule block, and change the border to `border-top: 1px solid var(--color-border-light)` for a clean neutral separator. Full replacement: `.health-alert-issue + .health-alert-issue { border-top: 1px solid var(--color-border-light); }` — delete the 4-line `> *` block entirely.

summary: Rework: fixed CSS opacity separator bug flagged in code review. Replaced the dead-code pattern (.health-alert-issue + .health-alert-issue { opacity: 0.6 } + .health-alert-issue + .health-alert-issue > * { opacity: calc(1/0.6) }) with a simple neutral border separator: border-top: 1px solid var(--color-border-light). The broken pattern caused all issue rows after the first to render at 60% opacity with no way to restore it, because CSS opacity creates a compositing layer and is bounded [0,1] — the calc(1/0.6) counter on children clamped to 1.0 and had zero effect. The new pattern is correct, readable, and uses an existing CSS custom property.
